findings.description: The RDS instance explicitly sets `storage_encrypted = false`, leaving database files, snapshots, and automated backups unencrypted at rest.

`publicly_accessible = true` gives the RDS instance a public endpoint/addressing path. Although the shown security group currently limits MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, public exposure unnecessarily expands the attack surface and can become internet-reachable if network rules change.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports to `0.0.0.0/0`. This allows unrestricted outbound connections from the database, creating an exfiltration and command-and-control path if it is compromised.

The EC2 instance role grants `s3:*`, `ec2:*`, and `rds:*` on every resource. Compromise of the web instance or its role credentials would give an attacker broad control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources in the account.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written into a PHP configuration file. User data and instance configuration can be read by principals with instance describe access, exposing the credential beyond a dedicated secrets-management boundary.
